h: Walk in from town, finish at Bettys
p: Harlow Carr has been open as a garden since 1950, when the Northern Horticultural Society set up its trial ground here, and it joined the RHS in 2001. Those decades of testing plants in a tough northern climate mean the ideas you pick up here actually work in gardens up north, which is a big plus for anyone planting in Yorkshire.

Here's a lovely way to arrive: walk in from Harrogate town centre. The route runs through the Valley Gardens and on through the Pinewoods to the garden, making a pleasant stroll of a couple of miles. You'll work up an appetite and skip the hassle of parking.

Speaking of appetites, Harlow Carr has its own Bettys café tea room, so you can treat yourself to a proper Yorkshire cuppa and a cake after your wander. It's a popular spot, so expect a queue at busy times.

Allow two to three hours for the garden, longer if you stop for lunch or browse the plant centre and shop. Paths are generally good, and there's plenty for kids to do in the play areas between the grown-up bits. Each season brings something different, from spring blossom and summer borders to autumn colour and winter stems, so it's well worth coming back.

Harrogate itself is a handsome spa town that's made for a wander. The Stray, a huge sweep of open grassland, is great for a picnic, the Royal Pump Room museum tells the story of the spa waters, and the historic Turkish Baths are a treat. For a change of scene, the riverside town of Knaresborough, with its viaduct and castle ruins, is only a short hop away.
